newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Treasuries mixed in Tokyo, adjustment dominant.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries mixed in Tokyo, adjustment dominant.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were narrowly mixed by Tokyo midday on Friday, with position adjustment dominating ahead of the weekend, traders said.
Shorter-end Treasuries were slightly bid, but other prices were mostly weighed down following overnight rallies.

Traders said short-term sentiment had improved slightly, particularly after the U.S. consumer prices index came in below market expectations this week, but prices were still vulnerable as credit-tightening concerns persisted.
The key 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 94-14/32, yielding 7.07 percent, against 94-17/32 in New York.
The market was hesitant about taking fresh positions in the morning amid a dearth of incentives, they said.
In New York on Thursday, Treasuries ended moderately higher as another round of weak economic reports prompted the market's second rally in three days.

"The recent indicators signalled that inflation was not getting out of control, but the market undertone is still fragile," a brokerage trader said. "Further corrective buying could push up prices a bit, but sharp rises are not expected."
The June T-bond futures contract fell 2/32 from the previous close to 107-25/32.
